A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EditCtrl and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing and inpainting evaluations in Tables 1–2, adapter ablations in Table 3, and qualitative demonstrations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative transferability and failure-case results in Appendix B, Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: EditCtrl retains the frozen backbone, local adapter, temporal global embedder, staged losses, and editing procedures. The added LazyDiffusion discussion explains prior work; style-LoRA composition is an additional experimental configuration rather than a revised EditCtrl algorithm.

E1.justification: Training data and the VPBench-Edit, VPBench-Inp, and DAVIS evaluations are unchanged. Appendix B adds qualitative coverage of 21:9 ultrawide timelapse footage and explicit high-motion and oversized-mask failure scenarios.

E2.justification: New Figure 7 adds a qualitative comparison between EditCtrl and EditCtrl augmented with DiffSynth-Studio's aesthetic LoRA. The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged; the new failure analysis reuses VACE.

E3.justification: The added appendix experiment evaluates editing with and without an aesthetic LoRA while retaining the fixed 256×256 global context. Existing benchmark metrics, training budgets, sampling settings, and throughput measurement procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a qualitative test of compressed-context adequacy and LoRA compatibility, plus high-motion and inaccurate-mask failure analyses. The original local/global adapter ablations in Table 3 and Figure 6 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added qualitative examples introduce no uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are identical. New Figures 7–8 report qualitative results for ultrawide editing, aesthetic-LoRA composition, shared high-motion artifacts with VACE, and excessive content changes under oversized masks.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit mathematical definition of LazyDiffusion's context-concatenated masked objective in Equation 3. EditCtrl's own objectives remain equivalent despite notation and numbering changes; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction refines the novelty framing by explicitly presenting EditCtrl as extending efficient image-editing principles to temporally coherent video through frozen-backbone adapters. The abstract and conclusion retain the same principal efficiency, quality, and interactive-editing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B interprets the ultrawide/LoRA example as supporting context adequacy and transferability. It supplements the existing fast-motion/VAE limitation with a VACE comparison and newly identifies oversized masks as causing undesirable content changes.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the publicly available DiffSynth-Studio Wan2.1-1.3b-lora-aesthetics-v1 checkpoint and provides its resource reference for the added experiment. Existing training, hardware, preprocessing, and content-propagation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: LazyDiffusion's role is substantially recast across Sections 1–3.1: v1 groups it with criticized compression approaches, whereas v2 explicitly credits it as a foundation and distinguishes EditCtrl through temporal video modeling and frozen-backbone adapters. A DiffSynth-Studio reference is also added.

P1.justification: Several introductory, related-work, and methodology paragraphs are rewritten. Section 3.1 gains background headings and the LazyDiffusion explanation; Section 3.2 consolidates its numbered adapter subsections. Appendix B expands, while most experimental prose and the conclusion remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds appendix Figures 7–8 and relocates the existing augmented-reality illustration as Figure 9. Earlier appendix Figures 8–13 become Figures 10–15 without changed images. Table 3 and Figure 6 also move; existing table structures and figure designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the contribution's relationship to LazyDiffusion and adds useful evidence about compatibility and failure conditions in Appendix B. This improves attribution and transparency. The gains remain limited: the new evidence consists of qualitative cases, with broad transferability and VAE-causality interpretations not independently established by those examples; the core method and quantitative validation are unchanged.
